training_and_serving_are_separate_planes.rationale: Training is a job that exits; serving is a process that must stay up. They differ in resource shape (a fit spikes memory, an inference does not), in scaling (train scales to zero, serving needs a warm replica), and in failure handling (a job retries, a service must stay available). Running a fit inside the serving process couples them at the worst point: the fit's memory spike is charged to the same cgroup as the live model cache, so a retrain can OOM-kill the endpoint that is currently answering. The trainer image also carries fit-time dependencies a serving process never calls, which is dead weight on every cold start.
training_and_serving_are_separate_planes.consequence: POST /retrain never fits anything itself. It records intent and returns; the existing trainer image does the work, spawned the same way MODEL-FLOW-003-T04 already spawns it.
training_and_serving_are_separate_planes.scope_correction: NARROWED 2026-08-25. This decision remains right for a long-running synchronous serving process (MODEL-SERVE-002) and for never fitting inside one. It was over-applied when written: it was read as 'inference always needs its own image', and scheduled batch inference is a counterexample its own rationale does not cover. See short_lived_containers_for_scheduled_inference. MODEL-SERVE-002-T01 (a separate serving image) is unaffected and stays.

deploy_is_a_row_change_not_an_image_buil.chosen: One generic serving image; the production pointer lives in Postgres
deploy_is_a_row_change_not_an_image_buil.rationale: The alternative — one image per model — makes every retrain a CI run and every rollback a redeploy, and turns N models into N deployments to operate. Since the model is data the process loads, not code it links against, the version in production is a fact about a row. Promotion becomes an UPDATE and rollback becomes the same UPDATE in reverse, which is what makes rollback fast enough to actually use during an incident.

short_lived_containers_for_scheduled_inf.chosen: Short-lived containers on the existing trainer image, second entrypoint
short_lived_containers_for_scheduled_inf.rationale: REVISES the scope of training_and_serving_are_separate_planes rather than contradicting it. That decision's reason is specific: a FIT spikes memory and, sharing a cgroup with a long-running cache, can OOM-kill the endpoint currently answering. Hourly batch inference is not a long-running process and holds no cache, so that reason does not apply to it. What is left is a comparison the existing code wins outright — trainning-container.authorized.service.ts already spawns, resource-limits and reaps containers; ModelTrainingRunLog and the /log callback already give per-run logs; image_digest provenance already comes for free. A second entrypoint (infer.py) beside train.py in images/trainer/ reuses all of it. Cold start is a python import, 3-5s, which is noise at a one-hour cadence.
short_lived_containers_for_scheduled_inf.consequence: MODEL-SERVE-006 needs no serving process, no cache-invalidation-on-promote, and no readiness protocol. Those belong to MODEL-SERVE-002 (synchronous /predict) alone, which is a SEPARATE requirement arriving later — do not build a serving service in order to get an hourly run.
short_lived_containers_for_scheduled_inf.also: One image, not two, additionally removes a divergence risk the two-image plan created: both entrypoints unpickle the same model.joblib, so they cannot disagree about the library that wrote it.

metrics_are_derived_from_predictions_not.chosen: predictions.parquet is the source of truth; metrics.json is a cache
metrics_are_derived_from_predictions_not.rationale: The alternative — the client sends a metric set and the container computes exactly those — has one failure that gets worse over time: adding a metric next month leaves every existing run without it, so a comparison table shows a column of em-dashes, and the only way to fill it is to RETRAIN models in order to compute a number that never needed a fit. Deriving from the stored predictions instead means a new metric is recomputable across all history, and the same definitions serve both evaluation (test-split predictions) and monitoring (inference predictions) — one implementation, so 'r2 at training' and 'r2 in monitoring' cannot drift into two numbers that look comparable and are not.
metrics_are_derived_from_predictions_not.constraint: STATE THE BOUNDARY EXPLICITLY IN THE REGISTRY. Only metrics computable from (actual, predicted) plus scalars already in run_manifest.json (e.g. feature_count for adjusted R²) are backfillable. Anything needing feature values, residual-vs-feature structure or model internals is NOT, and must be marked so — otherwise the registry mixes metrics that can be added retroactively with metrics that cannot, in one table, and nobody can tell which is which.

ORIGINAL, PRESERVED: 'NEW 2026-09-01, OPENED BY MODEL-SERVE-000-T07, NOT RESOLVED HERE — an audit surfaces the tension, MODEL-SERVE-001 decides it. But DS-LAKE-025's `adopt_artifact`... is live, working precedent for the OPPOSITE principle... Both are correct in their own scope and they point opposite directions on the same question.'
open_question_pin_by_pointer_or_copy_byt.rationale: The two precedents are not actually in tension once the difference in what each one is protecting is named. DS-LAKE-025 copies bytes OUT OF `drafts/` because the SOURCE prefix (a DatasetDraft's own workspace) is reclaimable — a dataset draft's sweeper can and does delete `drafts/{draftId}/...` once abandoned, so the saved Dataset must own independent bytes or a later reclaim takes it down. MODEL-SERVE-000-T07 measured the opposite fact for models: the FINAL artifact every run trains against is ALREADY unconditionally excluded from the cleanup candidate query (`artifact-cleanup.admin.service.ts`'s `where: { type: { not: 'FINAL' } }`), and an adopted run's own prefix (`drafts/{draftId}/runs/{runId}/...`) is protected by MODEL-FLOW-011-T05's adopted-run guard. There is no reclaimable source for a copy to protect against — copying would duplicate storage against a risk that does not exist, and it would violate MODEL-FLOW-007-T10's adopt-by-pointer rule for the same reason that rule exists on the training side: the row records what happened, it is not a workspace, and a copy is a second, driftable copy of facts the run row already owns.

rejected.Copy goldObjectKey/model.joblib/feature_: Rejected per the rationale above — no reclaimable source exists for models the way `drafts/{draftId}/artifacts/...` is reclaimable for an abandoned DatasetDraft, so the DS-LAKE-025 justification does not transfer. Revisit ONLY if a future change makes FINAL artifacts or adopted-run prefixes reclaimable while a ModelVersion still references them — at which point this decision inherits DS-LAKE-025's own reasoning instead of contradicting it.

open_question_pin_by_pointer_or_copy_byt.implementation: `ModelVersion.goldArtifactId/goldObjectKey/artifactChecksum/featureSpecKey/modelObjectKey` are copied as STRING KEYS from `ModelTrainingRun`'s own pinned columns at version-creation time (one hop, per MODEL-SERVE-000-T03/T07) — the row never re-derives through the dataset's current artifact, and it never fetches or duplicates the underlying bytes.

findings: CORRECTED 2026-08-24 FROM A MINIO SCREENSHOT OF A REAL RUN (bucket `datasets`, key drafts/1ce30923-394b-4135-b324-0e913606dcf9/runs/61f9aa28-0c31-4e99-bd52-4674200f72f6/, timestamps 2026-08-19 11:44 — one of the two runs MODEL-FLOW-003-V01 live-verified). The prior finding called the run's descriptor `manifest.json`; the object is `run_manifest.json`. The rename is not cosmetic: the name scopes it to the RUN, and a run descriptor and a serving descriptor are not the same document. A run manifest records what happened during a fit; serving needs what is required to LOAD the result. They may overlap, but assuming they are identical is exactly the kind of assumption MODEL-SERVE-000 exists to stop. Contents remain UNVERIFIED — the screenshot shows names and sizes only.

CORRECTED 2026-09-01 (MODEL-SERVE-000-T03). ORIGINAL CLAIM, PRESERVED: 'NEW AND HIGHEST SEVERITY IN THIS LEDGER — THE RUN DIRECTORY IS NOT A SELF-CONTAINED SERVING BUNDLE, CONFIRMED BY OBSERVATION. The directory holds exactly four objects: metrics.json (155 B), model.joblib (1.1 KiB), predictions.parquet (24.9 KiB), run_manifest.json (1.2 KiB). There is NO feature_spec.json and NO scaler or preprocessor object. model.joblib at 1.1 KiB is corroborating evidence rather than proof, but it is strong: a fitted sklearn Pipeline carrying a scaler's own state does not serialise to a kilobyte — this is an estimator alone. So a serving process cannot open this prefix and predict. It must resolve Model -> ModelTrainingRun -> DatasetArtifact.featureSpecKey -> feature_spec.json, three hops across two entities, and the transform state (scalers, the effective column list from select_columns + force_keep_target) lives at the far end of that chain on an entity the USER CAN EDIT.' THE 'THREE HOPS' CLAIM IS WRONG — read from packages/prisma/prisma/schema.prisma:1006-1031: ModelTrainingRun carries goldArtifactId, goldObjectKey, artifactChecksum AND featureSpecKey directly on the run row, set at launch from the ARTIFACT the run was actually created against (model-run-launch.authorized.service.ts:126, `featureSpecKey: artifact.featureSpecKey`) — never re-derived through the dataset's current artifact. Verified against the live dev database: 0 of 73 ModelTrainingRun rows have a null featureSpecKey. So this is ONE hop off the run row (ModelTrainingRun.featureSpecKey -> feature_spec.json), not three hops through an editable dataset. The 'not co-located, so a correct implementation can still be fed the wrong spec' exposure the finding worried about does not exist: the pinned key cannot silently repoint to an edited dataset's current artifact.

CORRECTED 2026-09-01 (MODEL-SERVE-000-T07). ORIGINAL CLAIM, PRESERVED: 'NEW — NOTHING PINS OR PROTECTS THE ARTIFACT A MODEL WAS FITTED AGAINST. MODEL-FLOW-010's own finding states that editing a dataset keeps the Dataset id and moves currentArtifactId, and correctly concludes that ModelDraft.datasetId stays valid. That conclusion is right for the WIZARD and wrong to inherit here: a served model needs the SPECIFIC artifact it was fitted against, not the dataset's current one, and neither ledger says that artifact is retained for as long as a model references it. Two separate objects can therefore be reclaimed out from under one production model — its bytes (guarded upstream by MODEL-FLOW-011-T05) and its feature spec (guarded by nothing). Losing either is the same outage.' WRONG ON BOTH CLAUSES, verified against schema.prisma and the live dev DB/MinIO. PINNING: ModelTrainingRun already carries goldArtifactId, goldObjectKey, artifactChecksum and featureSpecKey — an id-only reference was never the design (see schema.prisma:1019-1031's own comment: 'NOT how the container resolves data ... an id-only reference would silently retrain on different rows later'). PROTECTION: measured live — ALL 73 ModelTrainingRun rows train against a FINAL artifact, zero against GOLD. `artifact-cleanup.admin.service.ts`'s candidate query (`where: { type: { not: 'FINAL' } }`) and `artifact-cleanup-eligibility.ts:236` (`if (artifact.type === 'FINAL') continue`) both exclude FINAL unconditionally — it is never a cleanup candidate. Post-DS-LAKE-025, FINAL owns its bytes outright at `{datasetId}/artifacts/{artifactId}/` with feature_spec.json copied alongside (`adopt_artifact`, artifact_service.py:1268). 0 of 61 SUCCEEDED runs point at a missing or objectReclaimedAt-stamped artifact (measured). TWO REAL EXPOSURES SURVIVE, NEITHER THE ONE ORIGINALLY CLAIMED: (1) the FINAL protection is a TYPE EXCLUSION, not a ModelTrainingRun reference check — nothing but PreprocessingJob (QUEUED/RUNNING) counts as a live reference in the cleanup sweep, and `artifact-cleanup-eligibility.ts:314-324` explicitly allows GOLD/SILVER to age out 'even if still lineage-reachable', reasoning that an unreached one is storage 'nothing can ever reclaim and nothing reads' — false the moment a ModelTrainingRun points at it, which no launch path currently forbids. Latent, not live, today. (2) `deleteDatasetService` (apps/backend/src/api/v1/dataset/authorized/dataset.authorized.service.ts:234-246) checks ownership only, then `prisma.dataset.delete` — Dataset cascades onto DatasetArtifact (schema.prisma:563), and ModelTrainingRun.goldArtifactId is a bare String with no FK, so it dangles silently. Bytes still resolve (goldObjectKey/featureSpecKey are pinned keys, not FKs), but the objects become permanently unreclaimable — cleanup enumerates DatasetArtifact rows, and the row is gone. UPSTREAM TICKETS NAMED, NOT WRITTEN HERE: deleteDatasetService should refuse or warn when a ModelTrainingRun references the dataset's artifacts; the cleanup sweep's live-reference set should include ModelTrainingRun.goldArtifactId before any launch path can target a non-FINAL artifact.

NEW — ONE BUCKET HOLDS EVERYTHING. Model run outputs live in the `datasets` bucket (17.4 MiB / 138 objects at the time of the screenshot). That is fine today and cheap to leave alone, but it means no bucket-scoped lifecycle rule, retention policy or access grant can distinguish a production model's bytes from an abandoned dataset draft's. Anyone who later writes a lifecycle rule intending it for datasets writes it for models too. Record it now so that decision is made deliberately rather than discovered.

NEW AND USEFUL — MODEL-SERVE-002-V01 IS RUNNABLE TODAY. predictions.parquet exists in the run directory (24.9 KiB), so the no-skew test — score a row from the model's own test split through the live endpoint and assert it matches the recorded prediction — has real reference data against a real fitted model, with no live wizard and no MODEL-FLOW-007 required. This is the one verification in this ledger that can be built before its own dependencies land, and it is also the most load-bearing.

NEW — NO CHECKSUM SIDECAR EXISTS. There is no .sha256 or equivalent object beside model.joblib, so a checksum either lives inside run_manifest.json or is not computed at all. MODEL-SERVE-000-T01 must distinguish those two, because they lead to different work: reading a field, versus adding a write to the trainer AND accepting that every artifact predating that change has no checksum and needs a stated policy.

CONFIRMED 2026-08-24 by reading run_manifest.json from the run in the screenshot. The prior finding, and MODEL-SERVE-000-T01's three questions, are now answered and the finding is REPLACED rather than deleted so the audit trail survives: (1) a checksum EXISTS — model_sha256, plus artifact_checksum for the GOLD parquet; (2) provenance is pinned by image_digest (scgc/soft-sensor-trainer@sha256:…), which is STRONGER than the sklearn/joblib version string this ledger asked for, because it pins the whole runtime rather than one library; (3) the manifest does NOT carry a featureSpecKey, but it DOES inline feature_columns, target_y, target_scaled and derived_from_target — four of the fields serving would otherwise have walked to the spec for. seed and the full split record (method, ratio, cut_timestamp, labelled/train/test rows) are also present. This manifest is materially better than this ledger assumed, and the earlier UNVERIFIED framing overstated the gap.

CORRECTED 2026-09-01 (MODEL-SERVE-000-T03), PREMISE INVERTED. ORIGINAL CLAIM, PRESERVED: 'NARROWED 2026-08-24 — THE ONLY MISSING SERVING INPUT IS SCALER STATE. With feature_columns inlined, the three-hop chain to feature_spec.json collapses to one open question rather than a general dependency: where does a run's SCALER configuration live, and is it recoverable at serve time? The manifest records target_scaled: false, which proves the system tracks scaling on the target side, and records nothing about the feature side. model.joblib at 1.1 KiB for a bare 8-feature OLS is consistent with this particular run having no scalers at all — which is why it cannot answer the question. MODEL-SERVE-000-T03 must therefore be run against a run that DID scale, not this one; the smallest, cleanest artifact is the least informative one here.' SCALER STATE IS NOT MISSING. feature_spec.json carries `scalingParams` — the actual FITTED params per tag (e.g. `{"TI-101": {"min": 70.0, "max": 75.0}}`), written by artifact_service.features() / feature_spec_service.py:241. ModelTrainingRun.featureSpecKey pins the exact spec (schema.prisma:1031), verified non-null on 73/73 runs. The primitive that applies a FITTED transform to new rows without re-fitting already exists and is tested: `to_model_ready(frame, tags, scalers, fitted_params=scaling_params)`, wrapped by `prepare_holdout_for_run`/`replay_holdout_for_run` (artifact_service.py:570-706), which already REFUSES when a tag would scale without a recorded scalingParams entry (artifact_service.py:676-687) rather than silently re-fitting. Serving's answer to 'call it or extract it' (MODEL-SERVE-000-T03's own question) is CALL IT — these entry points are object-storage-keyed (`store.get_frame(source_key)`), which fits MODEL-SERVE-006's parquet windows directly; a synchronous row-list /predict needs a thin in-memory wrapper, not an extraction. WHY THE ORIGINAL INFERENCE FAILED: the run examined had `target_scaled: false` and a 1.1 KiB model.joblib, read as 'no scalers at all'. Both premises are true and the conclusion is false — feature_spec_service.py:250 sets `target_scaled` from `scalers.get(target_y, "none")` (the TARGET defaults to none), while feature_service.py:79 sets `DEFAULT_SCALER = "minmax"` (FEATURES default to minmax). Two different defaults in one document. The joblib is small because scalers were never in the pickle — they live in the spec, not the model object. See the new empty-`scaling` finding below for the trap this created.

NEW 2026-09-01 (MODEL-SERVE-000-T03), HIGHEST-SEVERITY FINDING OF THIS AUDIT PASS — THE EMPTY-`scaling` TRAP. feature_service.py:79 sets `DEFAULT_SCALER = "minmax"`. feature_spec_service.py's `scaling` array (line ~23) holds one `{tag, method}` entry ONLY for a tag with an EXPLICIT scaler choice — a tag left at the default writes NOTHING to `scaling`, even though it IS scaled. Measured directly against all 21 `feature_spec.json` objects currently in MinIO: every single one has `len(scaling) == 0` while `len(scalingParams) == 22`. So on every real dataset in this system, every tag is minmax-scaled by default, and `scaling: []` is exactly what that looks like on disk — indistinguishable, by that field alone, from 'nothing was scaled'. A serving process that reads `scaling` to decide whether to transform inputs, finds it empty, and concludes no scaling is needed will feed RAW values into a model fitted on SCALED inputs and return a plausible wrong number — silently, with no error, no missing field, nothing to alert on. The existing preprocessing code is safe today only because `to_model_ready` reads `scalers.get(tag, DEFAULT_SCALER)`, never `scaling` directly. Any new serving code (MODEL-SERVE-002-T05, MODEL-SERVE-006-T03) MUST resolve each tag's scaler the same way — from `scalingParams`' keys and/or the same default-aware lookup — never by branching on whether `scaling` is non-empty.

NEW 2026-09-01 (MODEL-SERVE-000-T04) — SERVABILITY CENSUS AGAINST LIVE DATA. Read all 21 `feature_spec.json` objects in MinIO and cross-referenced against the live dev Postgres: 0 of 21 specs have a non-empty `derived_from_target` (the target-history request-contract fork in MODEL-SERVE-002-T06 guards a class the schema permits but no real spec currently uses); 0 of 21 have `target_scaled: true`; exactly 1 of 21 has zero `scalingParams` entries and is therefore UNSERVABLE without re-fitting — and it is `drafts/c47bfa69-.../artifacts/b9e25f8d-.../feature_spec.json`, the exact artifact this ledger's own MinIO screenshot and repeated findings are built from (it predates DS-LAKE-018-T02, so it has no recorded fitted params). The coverage guard in `prepare_holdout_for_run` (artifact_service.py:676-687) already refuses to serve it rather than silently re-fitting, which is the correct behaviour. This ledger's most-cited example run is its ONLY unservable one, which is worth knowing before anyone scopes MODEL-SERVE-002 against it as a representative case.

IMAGE_DIGEST CREATES A NEW RETENTION DEPENDENCY. Pinning by digest is the right call, but a digest pins nothing once the image is garbage-collected from the registry — at which point the ONLY record of the runtime a production model was fitted under is a string that resolves to nothing. Whatever retains the model object and its artifact must extend to the trainer image any live ModelVersion names. This dependency did not exist under the version-string approach this ledger originally proposed; it is a consequence of the better mechanism, not a defect in it.

CORRECTED 2026-09-01 (MODEL-SERVE-000-T06). ORIGINAL CLAIM, PRESERVED: 'NEW — `drafts/` IS A SHARED ROOT FOR TWO UNRELATED ENTITIES IN ONE BUCKET. Observed directly: the run lives at drafts/1ce30923-…/runs/… (a ModelDraft) while its gold_object_key reads drafts/c47bfa69-…/artifacts/… (a DatasetDraft). Same bucket, same first segment, different tables, different lifecycles, different sweepers... The exposure is in the SWEEPERS... it is UNVERIFIED whether [DS-LAKE-014's DatasetDraft sweeper] reclaims by structural predicate or by a drafts/{id}/ prefix. If the latter, a dataset sweep can reach a model draft's prefix.' NOT REAL, confirmed by reading both call paths. This is a DIFFERENT endpoint from the model side's `/v1/preprocess/models/runs/reclaim` -> `reclaim_draft_runs`, which independently scopes to `drafts/{draftId}/runs/[{runId}/]` (artifact_service.py:1241-1264) and never a bare `drafts/{draftId}/`. Neither sweeper derives its prefix from a shared or naive draftId-only guess; each is keyed off its own row's structural data. No upstream ticket needed.

NEW — NOTHING GATES PROMOTION ON WHETHER THE MODEL IS ANY GOOD. The observed run has r2 = -2.4068: worse than predicting the mean, i.e. no predictive value. Every claim made about it is nonetheless true — MODEL-FLOW-003-V01 correctly recorded it as SUCCEEDED with real metrics, and the leakage guard correctly found nothing to check (derived_from_target is empty, so there is no leakage; the model is simply bad). MODEL-FLOW-000-T02 hardened this codebase against an implausibly HIGH R², and this is the opposite direction, which no criterion in either ledger covers. MODEL-SERVE-001-T05 refuses a version whose artifact cannot be LOADED; it says nothing about one that loads fine and is useless. See MODEL-SERVE-001-T06.

SUPERSEDED 2026-09-01 (MODEL-SERVE-000, upstream re-read). CONSEQUENCE...: r2 = -2.4068 is invisible in the product... every MODEL-FLOW-004 task is still pending.' NO LONGER TRUE. The wizard is now SIX phases, not four; the file this finding names no longer exists under that path — `phase-5-evaluation.tsx` (apps/client/app/(default)/models/create/components/pipeline/phase-5-evaluation.tsx) imports `useDraftRunEvaluation` and `mpTrainingResultAtom` and reads the run's real predictions, not a browser-side single-feature fit. tasks.detail:
OPENED 2026-08-24 from the observation that feature_spec.json is not in the run directory. features.title: Model Version Registry — One Row Decides What Is In Production
features.description: Give a Model a versioned, staged history so that promotion and rollback are row changes. Nothing here serves anything; this is the pointer everything downstream reads.

tasks.title: ModelVersion entity
tasks.detail: Shape depends on MODEL-SERVE-000-T02. Fields: modelId, version, the artifact pointer and checksum, feature spec reference, framework + version, sourceRunId, sourceDatasetId, metrics, stage, timestamps, promotedById. A version row is IMMUTABLE except for stage — same discipline as MODEL-FLOW-007-T10's adopt-by-pointer: the row records what happened, it is not a workspace.
tasks.detail_addendum: REVISED 2026-08-24: the artifact reference is NOT optional and NOT derivable later. Because the run directory holds no feature spec (see findings), ModelVersion must record the fitted DatasetArtifact's id and its featureSpecKey explicitly, alongside the model object pointer. Resolving it at serve time by walking to the dataset's CURRENT artifact would be silently wrong for any model whose dataset was edited after training — and it would be wrong in the direction that still returns a number.
tasks.audit_2026_09_01: MODEL-SERVE-000 confirmed the run row already stores exactly this (ModelTrainingRun.goldArtifactId/goldObjectKey/artifactChecksum/featureSpecKey, verified non-null on 73/73 runs) — this task copies those four fields onto ModelVersion at promotion-worthy points, it does not invent them. Also: decisions.open_question_pin_by_pointer_or_copy_bytes is now open and must be resolved as part of this task — does ModelVersion reference the source artifact by pointer (per MODEL-FLOW-007-T10's adopt-by-pointer rule) or copy its bytes into a version-owned prefix (per DS-LAKE-025's adopt_artifact precedent)? Record the choice in that decision with its rejected alternative.
tasks.result_2026_09_01: COMPLETED. `ModelVersion` model + `ModelVersionStage` enum added to schema.prisma (migration 20260901090000_model_serve_001_model_version), migrated and verified against the live dev DB. decisions.open_question_pin_by_pointer_or_copy_bytes resolved POINTER with rejected alternative recorded (see that decision). FOUND AND FIXED DURING IMPLEMENTATION, NOT PART OF THE ORIGINAL SPEC: (1) the migration's `ModelVersion_sourceRunId_fkey` was originally `ON DELETE RESTRICT` — verified live (rolled-back transaction, then a real cascade-delete of a seeded Model+run+version) that this breaks `deleteModelService` (`model.authorized.service.ts`'s bare `prisma.model.delete`), because a Model delete cascades onto BOTH ModelTrainingRun and ModelVersion in one statement and RESTRICT is checked immediately per-row rather than deferred to end-of-statement. Changed to `NO ACTION` in both the migration and schema.prisma, migration dropped and cleanly reapplied (table was empty, zero data loss) since it had already been applied by an earlier session with the broken FK. Re-verified live: a real `DELETE FROM "Model"` with a full Model+run+version chain now cascades cleanly. (2) `model_sha256` — needed for `ModelVersion.modelChecksum` — was NOT actually a `ModelTrainingRun` column despite three docstrings (RunManifestRequest, RunManifestResponse's router description, get_run_manifest) all claiming it was; verified against schema.prisma and fixed at the source: `get_run_manifest`/`RunManifestResponse` now read and return it from run_manifest.json (same honest-legacy-null policy as framework_versions), all three stale docstrings corrected in place. Live-verified against a real run's manifest: `model_sha256` now returns `'b5d52d61150a161...117065'` where it previously silently returned nothing. Save Model (T03) now populates version 1's `modelChecksum` from this.

tasks.title: Stage machine and the single-production constraint
tasks.detail: STAGING -> PRODUCTION -> ARCHIVED. Enforce at most one PRODUCTION per modelId AT THE DATABASE, with a partial unique index, not in service code. Application-level uniqueness under concurrent promotes is the same class of hole MODEL-FLOW-007-T10's 409 guard closes for double-save, and the same reason MODEL-FLOW-002-T07 used a CHECK constraint rather than a service check.
tasks.result_2026_09_01: COMPLETED. `ModelVersion_one_production_per_model`, a partial unique index (`ON ("modelId") WHERE stage = 'PRODUCTION'`), same hand-written-migration precedent as `ModelFineTuningJob_one_live_per_draft` — Prisma's schema DSL cannot express a partial index. The pure stage-transition predicate lives at `apps/backend/src/lib/model-version-transitions.ts` (`isPromotable`), mirroring `dataset-version-transitions.ts`'s shape but a DIFFERENT graph: ARCHIVED -> PRODUCTION is legal here (a rollback is a promote), which the dataset side's strict forward line does not allow — documented in that file's own doc comment. Live-proven under real concurrency in V01 (see verification).

tasks.title: Save Model creates version 1 in STAGING, never PRODUCTION
tasks.detail: Saving is not deploying. A wizard whose last click puts a model in front of live traffic has no step at which someone decides it should be. This is additive to MODEL-FLOW-007-T04's transaction, inside the same transaction — a Model with no version row is a state nothing downstream can interpret.
tasks.result_2026_09_01: COMPLETED. `ModelDraftAuthorizedService.saveDraftService` (model-draft.authorized.service.ts) now creates `ModelVersion` version 1 inside the SAME `$transaction` as the `Model` create and the `ModelTrainingRun`/`ModelDraft` updates — no separate write, no window where a Model can exist without a version row. `version: 1` is hardcoded (not max()+1: `created` is a brand-new Model in this same transaction, so no other version can exist yet — a future retrain minting a later version needs DS-LAKE-009-T03's max()+1 allocation, this path does not). `stage` is never set on create, so it takes the schema's `STAGING` default — verified live via V01's seed rows (queried back as STAGING before any promote). Fields are copied one-hop from the adopted `ModelTrainingRun` row's own pinned columns, never re-derived through the dataset's current artifact.

tasks.title: Promote and rollback endpoints
tasks.detail: POST .../versions/:v/promote and POST .../rollback, both recording who and when. Rollback is promote pointed at the previous PRODUCTION — not a distinct mechanism, so it cannot rot separately. Envelope per the findings.
tasks.result_2026_09_01: COMPLETED. New module `apps/backend/src/api/v1/model-version/` (mirroring the model-run/model-draft/model-draft-cleanup convention of one module per feature despite tight coupling to Model), registered in `app.module.ts`. `POST authorized/model/:modelId/versions/:version/promote` (`:version` is the integer version number, not the row id — a human-operable natural key given `@@unique([modelId, version])`) and `POST authorized/model/:modelId/rollback`. Both funnel through one private `promote()` method — rollback resolves the most-recently-`archivedAt` ARCHIVED row and calls the SAME gate (T05 object check, T06 r2 floor), per the feature's own 'not a distinct mechanism' decision. Both record `promotedById`/`promotedAt`. Standard `{statusCode, message, type, data}` envelope, editor-level access (`assertModelAccess`, same rule as every other mutating Model route). An already-PRODUCTION promote is an idempotent no-op, matching `isLegalTransition`'s own documented policy split on the dataset side. TIGHTENED DURING ADVISORY REVIEW: rollback's lookup originally read `where: { stage: 'ARCHIVED', archivedAt: { not: null } }` — correct only BY ABSENCE, since only `promote()` writes ARCHIVED today, not by construction. Added `promotedAt: { not: null }` (set only by `promote()`'s own transaction) so a version that reaches ARCHIVED through some future path without ever having been PRODUCTION cannot become a rollback target. Also: the override's `actorName` was `user.email` — changed to the same firstName/lastName-then-fallback resolution `updateModelService`'s `editorName` already uses, so a promotion override records the same identity string as the rest of the Model audit trail rather than a login email.

tasks.title: Refuse to promote a version whose artifact cannot be loaded
tasks.detail: Verify object existence and checksum BEFORE flipping the stage. A promote that succeeds against a missing or altered object turns a deploy into an outage discovered by the first request, and the rollback path is then also untested. This is the one place a slow check is worth it.
tasks.result_2026_09_01: COMPLETED. No existing primitive covered this — `/artifacts/presign` is hard-restricted to committed dataset artifacts (`is_committed_artifact_key`) and refuses `model.joblib` outright, so a new endpoint was added rather than reusing it: `POST /v1/preprocess/models/runs/verify-object` (`artifact_service.verify_model_object`, guarded by the same `is_draft_run_key`/`is_model_run_key` structural check `run_predictions`/`get_run_manifest` already use) returns `{exists, checksum}`, checksum computed from the object's own bytes via `store.checksum_of`. Backend wrapper `verifyModelObject` in `python-preprocess-client.ts`. `promote()` calls it BEFORE the transaction: refuses (422) if `!exists` unconditionally, and refuses (422) on a checksum mismatch ONLY when `ModelVersion.modelChecksum` is non-null. NAMED EXPLICITLY, NOT LEFT IMPLICIT (flagged in advisory review): `modelChecksum` is null for any version whose source run predates the manifest recording `model_sha256` — MODEL-SERVE-000-T04's own servability census found the ledger's own most-cited example run is exactly this shape — so for those versions the checksum half of this task's acceptance criterion does not apply; only existence is checked. This is the same honest-legacy-null policy `frameworkVersions` already established, not a gap introduced here, but the acceptance criterion 'promoting a version whose checksum does not match fails' holds unconditionally only for versions created after this change (i.e. every version going forward, since T01 now populates `modelChecksum` on every save whose manifest has it). LIVE-VERIFIED end to end against real MinIO (not mocked) for the primitive itself: wrote a real object, confirmed `exists:true` + a real sha256 checksum, deleted it, confirmed `exists:false, checksum:null`, and confirmed the structural guard refuses a non-run-shaped key (e.g. a dataset artifact path) by name rather than silently accepting it. See V02.

tasks.title: Refuse to promote a version whose metrics fail a floor, unless overridden on the record
tasks.detail:
OPENED 2026-08-24 after observing r2 = -2.4068 on a run this project's own live verification recorded as successful. A negative R² is not a marginal model, it is a model with no predictive value, and there is currently no boundary at which anyone is asked whether it should go to production.

The floor must be a REFUSAL, not a warning. A warning at promote time is read once by the person who already decided to promote, which is the moment it has least effect. Make r2 <= 0 a hard block; anything above that is a judgement call and belongs to the human, not to a threshold this task invents.

An override must be possible — a deliberately weak model has legitimate uses (a baseline to beat, a smoke test of the serving path) — but it must be RECORDED on the ModelVersion with an actor and a reason, so that 'why is this in production' has an answer six months later. An override that leaves no trace is the same as no floor.

DO NOT PUT THIS IN THE WIZARD INSTEAD. Step 4 Evaluation showing a negative R² prominently is good and separate; MODEL-FLOW-004 owns it. The promote boundary needs its own gate because promotion is reachable without the wizard — see MODEL-SERVE-001-T04's endpoints.

acceptance_criteria: Save Model produces exactly one ModelVersion at STAGING and no PRODUCTION version.
Two concurrent promotes against one model cannot both leave a PRODUCTION row — enforced by the database, proven by a concurrent test rather than by reading the service.
Rollback restores the previous PRODUCTION version and is recorded with an actor.
Promoting a version whose object is missing or whose checksum does not match fails and leaves the current PRODUCTION untouched.
A ModelVersion row's artifact pointer, checksum and metrics are never updated after creation.

verification.result_2026_09_01: LIVE-PROVEN against the real dev DB, at the SQL level rather than through the NestJS/auth stack (no backend server was running to exercise HTTP end to end; the actual mechanism under test — the partial unique index — is a DB-level guarantee, so a real concurrent DB test proves the acceptance criterion directly). Seeded one Model with two STAGING ModelVersions under two real ModelTrainingRun rows. Two concurrent `psql` sessions each opened a transaction and updated a DIFFERENT version to `stage='PRODUCTION'`, staggered so both UPDATEs landed before either committed. Observed: transaction A's UPDATE succeeded and committed; transaction B's UPDATE BLOCKED (Postgres's standard behavior for a value that might conflict with an uncommitted row), then on A's commit failed immediately with `duplicate key value violates unique constraint "ModelVersion_one_production_per_model"` and rolled back. Final state queried: exactly one PRODUCTION row (version-1), version-2 untouched at STAGING. This is precisely the P2002-on-that-constraint-name path `ModelVersionAuthorizedService`'s `promote()` catches and maps to a 409. Test rows cleaned up via `DELETE FROM "Model"` (cascades) — which also re-confirmed T01's FK fix live a second time.

features.title: Serving Runtime and Synchronous /predict
features.description: A long-running process that loads PRODUCTION versions from object storage and answers bounded synchronous prediction requests. One image, many models.

tasks.title: Serving image, without the trainer's fit-time dependencies
tasks.detail: Note the deployment-currency trap MODEL-FLOW-000-T04's verification_note already recorded for the trainer: nothing in CI builds images/trainer/Dockerfile, so repo source being correct proves nothing about what is deployed. Do not inherit that. The serving image gets a CI build from the first commit, or it acquires the same untraceable drift.

tasks.title: Multi-model loader with a bounded cache
tasks.detail_addendum: REVISED 2026-08-24: verify model_sha256 (the field name is now known, not hypothesised) and verify image_digest against the serving runtime — noting that a digest match is not achievable if serving runs a DIFFERENT image from the trainer, which decisions.training_and_serving_are_separate_planes deliberately requires. So the digest is a provenance record to CHECK FOR PRESENCE and log, not a value to match. What must actually be validated at load is that the serving runtime's own library versions are compatible with the pickle; the digest tells you what to go and look up when they are not.
tasks.detail: Resolve model_id -> PRODUCTION version -> object; verify checksum; verify the recorded framework version against the runtime and REFUSE on a mismatch rather than warn (see findings — a silently-loaded mismatch produces plausible wrong numbers). Cache bounded by memory, not by entry count: models differ in size by orders of magnitude and a count-based cap sizes for the smallest one.
tasks.audit_2026_09_01: MODEL-SERVE-000 found the loader must also resolve scaler state alongside the model object — read feature_spec.json's scalingParams via ModelTrainingRun.featureSpecKey (one hop, verified non-null on 73/73 runs) at the same load step, and resolve each tag's method the way to_model_ready does (scalers.get(tag, DEFAULT_SCALER)), never by checking whether the spec's `scaling` array is non-empty — see the empty-`scaling`-array trap finding, which is real and specific to this task.

tasks.title: Warm the production set before reporting ready
tasks.detail: /healthz answers without touching MinIO or Postgres (a liveness probe that depends on them turns a dependency blip into a restart loop); /readyz answers only after the production set is loaded. Getting this backwards means traffic arrives during cold load and the first caller pays for everyone.

tasks.title: POST /predict, bounded and validated against feature_spec.json
tasks.detail: Validate presence, dtype and column ORDER against the spec, and cap rows per request. Reject with a message naming the offending column. sklearn's own error on a mismatched frame names a column and explains nothing — the same complaint MODEL-FLOW-010-T07 makes about pyarrow's 'No match for FieldRef.Name' reaching a user who cannot act on it. The range checks the dataset wizard's feature presets already express are the natural source for a range warning here; reuse rather than restate.

tasks.title: Apply the training-time preprocessing, by calling it
tasks.detail: Per MODEL-SERVE-000-T03's answer. If the path is callable, call it. If it is not, extract it into a module BOTH the trainer and the server import, and make the trainer use the extracted copy in the same change — leaving the trainer on the original and the server on a copy is precisely the drift this task exists to prevent, and it would pass every test written against either side alone.
tasks.audit_2026_09_01: ANSWERED: call it. `to_model_ready(frame, tags, scalers, fitted_params=scaling_params)` (apps/python) already applies a fitted transform without re-fitting and is already tested via prepare_holdout_for_run/replay_holdout_for_run. It is frame-in/frame-out and object-storage-keyed today; a synchronous /predict needs a thin in-memory wrapper around it (rows -> frame -> to_model_ready -> rows), not an extraction. No new shared module is needed.

tasks.title: Refuse target-derived models that are not given target history
tasks.detail: Read derived_from_target at LOAD time and fix the request contract from it, rather than discovering the gap per-request. Also validate the submitted history's sampling interval against the spec. A model in this class served without history does not error — it predicts from imputed or absent lags and returns a number, which is the failure mode with no symptom.
tasks.audit_2026_09_01: Measured: 0 of 21 live feature_spec.json objects have a non-empty derived_from_target. This guard governs a class the schema permits but no real model in this system currently belongs to — keep the guard (schema allows it), but do not treat /predict's request-contract fork as validated against real data; it is untested against a real target-derived model because none exists yet.

tasks.title: Invalidate the cache on promote
tasks.detail: After a promote, replicas holding the old version keep serving it until something tells them. Whatever the mechanism (a short TTL on the version lookup is the cheapest and is probably enough), the CONTRACT is what matters: state the maximum time a promoted version can take to become live, and make it a number someone chose rather than an emergent property. Silent divergence between two replicas answering the same request differently is very hard to diagnose from the outside.

acceptance_criteria: A promoted model answers /predict with no image rebuild and no redeploy.
A request missing a required column is refused with that column named — not a 500 from the estimator.
A model whose feature spec is target-derived cannot be served without target history, and the refusal states why.
The transform applied at inference is the SAME CODE as the one applied at training, not an equivalent one.
A checksum or framework-version mismatch prevents a load; it never degrades to a warning.
/healthz does not depend on MinIO or Postgres; /readyz does.
After a promote, every replica serves the new version within the stated bound.

verification.description: PROVE NO SKEW, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT: take a row from the model's own test split, send it through /predict, and assert the prediction matches the value in that run's predictions artifact to numerical tolerance. Any test using synthetic input proves the endpoint returns a float, which is not the claim. This is the V02-of-MODEL-FLOW-000 of this ledger — the one verification whose absence would make everything else look fine.

Promote a new version while /predict is under continuous load and confirm every response is answerable by SOME valid version, with the switchover inside the stated bound and no request failing at the boundary.

Load a model whose feature spec declares a non-empty derived_from_target and confirm a history-less request is refused. Then submit history at the WRONG sampling interval and confirm it is also refused — a serving process that accepts the second has not implemented this task, only half of it.
Point the loader at an object whose bytes have been altered and confirm the load fails on checksum rather than succeeding.

features.title: Batch Prediction and Job Results
features.description: Score a parquet input in object storage as an asynchronous job, and return the result by reference. This is the '/predict + /result' pair from the original question, split because they are two different operations.

tasks.title: PredictionJob entity and its state machine
tasks.detail: QUEUED/RUNNING/SUCCEEDED/FAILED/CANCELED, mirroring ModelTrainingRun's vocabulary rather than inventing a parallel one. State in Postgres, never in process memory — MODEL-FLOW-003-V01's stranded run is the demonstration of what in-memory job tracking does across a restart, and a result endpoint answering 404 for a job that finished is the same bug with a friendlier face.

tasks.title: POST /predict:batch with an idempotency key
tasks.detail: Returns a job id immediately. The idempotency key is not optional: MODEL-FLOW-003-T09 had to add poll-failure tolerance specifically because a transient error pushed users toward a retry that would spawn a SECOND container against the same draft. A batch endpoint without a key has the identical hole and the same trigger.

tasks.title: Batch worker, chunked
tasks.detail: Stream the input rather than loading it whole. MODEL-FLOW-010-V03 exists because a single unbounded read at 8,000 tags produced 76MB where 489KB was needed; a batch scorer is the most likely place for that to reappear, and it will reappear on someone else's data, not in a test.

tasks.title: GET /jobs/:id — status, and the output by presigned reference
tasks.detail: Never stream result bytes through the API. Reuse the existing presign path (artifact_service.presign_artifact) rather than writing a second one, and honour MODEL-FLOW-000-T06's rule: neither the presign request nor the URL reaches a log, because the URL IS the capability.

tasks.title: Record which version scored the batch
tasks.detail: Pin the version at job START and store it on the job. A long batch spanning a promote must not silently score its first half on one model and its second on another — and a result whose model is 'whatever was production at some point' cannot be reproduced or defended later.

acceptance_criteria: The batch endpoint returns a job id without waiting for the work.
Job state survives a restart of the process that created it.
Results are delivered by presigned reference; no result bytes traverse the API.
The same idempotency key cannot produce two jobs.
Every job records the exact model version that scored it, pinned at start.
A batch over a wide input keeps memory bounded — no unbounded read of the input frame.

verification.description: Submit a batch, restart the serving process mid-flight, and confirm GET /jobs/:id still reports truthfully — either a completed job or a job that reached a terminal FAILED with a stated reason. Permanently RUNNING is the failure this checks for, and it is the exact state MODEL-FLOW-003-V01 observed on the training side.
Submit the same idempotency key twice concurrently and confirm one job. Sequential submission is a weaker test that a naive check would also pass.

Promote a new version DURING a running batch and confirm the output was scored end to end by the pinned version, asserted from the job row and the output's own recorded version — not inferred from timing.

tasks.detail: Three clicks must not become three containers competing for the same 8 GiB. MODEL-FLOW-000-T03 established that /scratch's tmpfs shares the container's memory cgroup, so concurrent fits are not merely slow, they are a plausible OOM.

tasks.detail: Per decisions.training_and_serving_are_separate_planes.

tasks.title: Compare the candidate against the incumbent, and publish the comparison

Concurrent triggers for one model produce one job.
A successful retrain creates a STAGING version and changes no PRODUCTION pointer.
The candidate-versus-incumbent comparison states its evaluation basis, and refuses to present a delta across incomparable bases as if it were one.

verification.description: Trigger a retrain and confirm PRODUCTION is unchanged after it succeeds. The point of the feature is what it does NOT do.
Fire three concurrent triggers and confirm one container. Count containers, not jobs — a service that dedupes the row but spawns three is the failure this guards.

features.title: Prediction Logging and Drift Signal
features.description: Record inputs and predictions so that a model going wrong is observable, and so that a future automatic retrain has a trigger that is a measurement rather than a calendar.

tasks.title: Log request features, prediction and version to the time-series store
tasks.detail: Sampled, not every request — full-fidelity logging of a high-rate soft sensor is a second data pipeline nobody planned for. State the sampling rate; a rate chosen by accident makes every downstream statistic uninterpretable.

tasks.title: Compare live input distributions against the training distribution
tasks.detail: The training distribution is already characterised — column_stats is the sidecar the dataset wizard writes and MODEL-FLOW-010-T04 reads. Compare against it rather than recomputing a baseline, so both surfaces agree on what 'normal' was.

tasks.title: Join late-arriving ground truth and track live error
tasks.detail: For a lab-sampled target the truth arrives hours or days later, so this is a delayed join, not a live metric. Publish the missing/Bad rate of the joined window beside the error, for the reason MODEL-FLOW-010-T06 gives: with no imputation, a hole depresses the score with no trace of why.

With MODEL-SERVE-006, the primary prediction stream is the hourly window record, which is complete rather than sampled and already carries version and missing rate. So T01's sampling concern applies to MODEL-SERVE-002's sync path only, and T02 (drift vs column_stats) and T03 (late ground-truth join) now read from InferenceWindow. features.title: Scheduled Hourly Inference — Windows, Logs, and the Monitoring Record
features.description: Run a promoted model on a fixed cadence, writing one predictions parquet and one metrics document per time window, with per-run logs readable afterwards. This is the feature that makes 'deployed' mean something. It needs no serving process — see decisions.short_lived_containers_for_scheduled_inference.

dependency_notes.MODEL-FLOW-004: SATISFIED 2026-09-01 (MODEL-SERVE-000 re-audit). ORIGINAL: 'HARD, not conventional. Step 4 currently computes its own metrics client-side (see findings), so until it reads the run's real metrics there is no surface on which a metric registry or a monitoring series means anything. Building the schedule first would produce a correct monitoring record beside a screen showing unrelated numbers.' MODEL-FLOW-004 is now in_progress 90 with all 5 tasks completed; phase-5-evaluation.tsx reads real predictions via useDraftRunEvaluation/mpTrainingResultAtom, not a client-side computeFit. T08 can proceed.
dependency_notes.MODEL-FLOW-011: SATISFIED 2026-09-01 (MODEL-SERVE-000 re-audit). ORIGINAL: 'Specifically T04, orphaned-RUNNING reconciliation. MODEL-FLOW-003-V01 observed ONE stranded RUNNING row from ONE nest restart. At 24 windows a day that stops being an incident and becomes a background rate, and every stranded row is a permanent hole in the monitoring record. Reconciliation must exist before the cadence does, not after.' MODEL-FLOW-011 is completed 100%, including T04 (reconcileOrphanedRuns() at boot, trainning-container.authorized.service.ts:53-123) and T05 (never reclaim an adopted run's prefix).
dependency_notes.MODEL-SERVE-002: NOT a dependency, deliberately. Synchronous /predict is a different requirement; this feature must not wait on it and must not build a serving process to get a scheduled run.

findings: THE UNIT IS A TIME WINDOW, NOT A TICK. A scheduler written as 'every hour, read the latest values, predict' loses data permanently on every miss, cannot say which hours are missing, and has no backfill path. A scheduler written as 'ensure a row exists for every window' gets gap detection, backfill and idempotency from one UNIQUE constraint. This is the single decision the whole feature rests on.

SCHEDULED WORK HAS NO CALLER, WHICH CHANGES WHAT FAILURE MEANS. A sync request that fails returns an error to someone who is waiting. A window that fails is observed by nobody. So the feature is not complete when windows succeed — it is complete when a window that DOESN'T run is visible. Hence T10, which is the one task here that must not be cut.

setInterval().unref() IS ADEQUATE HERE, BUT FOR A DIFFERENT REASON THAN IT WAS ADEQUATE FOR THE SWEEPER. MODEL-FLOW-011-T03 chose it because a missed sweep costs nothing — next tick does the work. A missed inference window is a permanent gap. It is still adequate, but ONLY because the tick's job is an idempotent insert keyed on window_start, so a later tick recovers what an earlier one missed. If the tick ever predicts directly, this mechanism becomes wrong.

PI TAGS DO NOT ARRIVE TOGETHER AND THE LAB TARGET ARRIVES MUCH LATER. window_end = now() yields a frame that is structurally complete and factually empty in places — and the model will score it without error, because the columns exist. This is the same mechanism MODEL-FLOW-010-T06 records for the holdout (no imputation, so a hole reaches predict() and depresses the result with no trace), except it recurs every hour instead of once. Hence a deliberate lag (T04) and a per-window missing rate (T05).

A PROMOTE MID-SERIES IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A PROCESS CHANGE UNLESS THE VERSION IS PINNED PER WINDOW. Two adjacent points from different model versions render as a step change on the same axis as a real process shift, and someone will spend days on the wrong hypothesis. Pinning also yields shadow evaluation for free: two rows, same window, different versions.

tasks.title: InferenceWindow entity, keyed on (modelVersionId, windowStart)
tasks.detail:
Fields: modelId, modelVersionId, windowStart, windowEnd, status (PENDING|RUNNING|SUCCEEDED|FAILED|SKIPPED), predictionsKey, metricsKey, inputRows, missingPct, imageDigest, runId, startedAt, finishedAt, failureReason.

UNIQUE (modelVersionId, windowStart) IS THE WHOLE DESIGN. It is the idempotency mechanism, so this feature needs no idempotency key of the kind MODEL-SERVE-003-T02 requires — windowStart is the natural key and a repeated insert is a no-op. It also makes gaps queryable (status != 'SUCCEEDED') and makes backfill an insert rather than a code path.

SKIPPED is a real terminal status, not a synonym for FAILED: a window with too few input rows to score was correctly not attempted, and conflating it with a failure would make the staleness alarm cry wolf on a quiet plant.

tasks.title: The tick inserts windows and nothing else
tasks.detail:
setInterval(...).unref() in onModuleInit, matching MODEL-FLOW-011-T03's mechanism and PreprocessingJobService.scheduleStragglerSweep's precedent. Env-configurable, <= 0 disables.

The tick does exactly two things: insert PENDING rows for windows that have none, and reconcile rows stuck in RUNNING past a timeout. IT MUST NOT SCORE ANYTHING. Scoring in the tick reintroduces every property this design exists to avoid — a missed tick becomes a lost window, the interval becomes load-bearing, and a slow run delays the next one. Errors logged and swallowed; anything the tick missed is still eligible next time, which is only true because of T01's key.

tasks.title: infer.py as a second entrypoint on the existing trainer image
tasks.detail:
Reads its window spec from a /claim-style callback exactly as train.py does, resolves the model object and scaler state (MODEL-SERVE-000-T03 must have answered where scalers live — this task is blocked in practice until it has), scores, writes predictions.parquet and metrics.json, reports through /log and /complete.

Same image as the trainer so both entrypoints unpickle with the same library versions, and so image_digest provenance works identically. HEED MODEL-FLOW-000-T04's warning: nothing in CI builds images/trainer/Dockerfile, so a correct repo and a stale deployed image are indistinguishable today. Adding an entrypoint makes that worse, because a deployed image without infer.py fails in a way that looks like a scheduler bug. Add the CI build in this task, not later.
